

### C and cache misses (struct, rewritten?)  {.smaller}


```c
int array[60];
int a_sum = 0, b_sum = 0;
for (int i = 0; i < 60; i += 12)
    a_sum += array[i];
for (int i = 1; i < 60; i += 12)
    b_sum += array[i];
```
 

* [Assume everything but <code>array</code> is kept in registers (and the compiler does not do anything funny) and array at beginning of cache block.]{.my-small}
* How many <i>data cache misses</i> on a 64B direct-mapped cache with 16B cache blocks?
* observation 1: first loop has 5 misses --- first accesses to each block
* observation 2: array[0] and array[1], array[12] and array[13], etc. in same cache block

### C and cache misses (struct, solution written)  {.smaller}


* ints 4 byte $\rightarrow{}$ array[0 to 3] and array[16 to 19] in same cache set 

   * 64B = 16 ints stored per way
   * 4 sets total

* accessing array indices 0, 12, 24, 36, 48, 1, 13, 25, 37, 49
   *  0, 12, 24, 36, 48 all misses

* 0 (set 0, array[0 to 3]), 12 (set 3, 12-15), 24 (set 2, 24-27), 36 (set 1, 36-39), 48 (set 0, 48-51) 

   *  13, 25, 37 will be hits (rest of block already loaded)
   *  1 will be a miss (0-3 was replaced with 48-51 when 48 accessed)
   *  49 will be a miss (48-51 was replaced with 0-3 when 1 accessed)

*
